For this Amice comparison only, R has an algebra structure over Z with continuous scalar action, as in the pinned Amice transform.
proofSteps: Apply the pinned coefficient formula to the existing Amice transform of P_(n,a)μ.
Use residue-restriction-evaluation on that fixed R-valued Mahler test. This is one coefficient at a time, with no interchange of an infinite sum and a measure.
acceptance: This coefficient identity is not the Fourier expression with p^n-th roots; convergence and integral descent for that expression remain separate targets.

nodes.title: Duals and biduals as intersections of localisations
nodes.statement: For a finite torsion-free module M over a noetherian normal domain A with fraction field K, the native bidual embeds in K⊗_A M, compatibly with the evaluation map from M. Its image equals the intersection of the images of the native localisations M_𝔭 for height-one primes 𝔭.
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: Lift M→K⊗_A M to each native localisation using invertibility of every allowed denominator. Take ranges in this single carrier.

Use localisation of Hom for finite presentations and freeness of torsion-free modules over the height-one DVRs. The resulting bidual embedding is fixed by its agreement with evaluation on M. Height-one DVRs, intersection of the rings and local Hom comparisons remain recorded proof inputs.
acceptance: Mathlib's Module.IsReflexive is the target notion; the intersection description is the new content.

hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: Localise away from the finite height-one torsion support to a semilocal PID, split the torsion summand there, and clear the projector denominator using localisation of Hom. The latter two proof inputs are gaps.

nodes.title: The reflexive hull is a pseudo-isomorphism
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated torsion-free A-module M, the bidual map φ_M : M → M⁺⁺ is an injective pseudo-isomorphism into a reflexive module (Proposition 5.1.8).
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: M_𝔭 is free over A_𝔭 for 𝔭 of height ≤ 1, so M_𝔭 → M_𝔭⁺⁺ is an isomorphism; M⁺⁺ is reflexive by Corollary 5.1.3; ker φ_M ⊗ K = 0, so ker φ_M is torsion inside a torsion-free module, hence zero.
acceptance: Free modules are their own reflexive hulls.

sources.match: Proposition 5.1.8 and its proof.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules over two-dimensional regular local rings are free
nodes.statement: Every finitely generated reflexive module over a two-dimensional regular local ring A is free.
hypotheses: A regular local of dimension n with 2 ≤ n < ∞, and integrally closed (automatic for regular local rings by Auslander–Buchsbaum, which is cited, not planned here).
proofSteps: For a regular parameter x, A/(x) is a DVR. The quotient of the bidual embeds in Hom_A(M⁺,A/(x)), so M/xM is torsion-free and free there. Lift a minimal presentation and use Nakayama twice. Regular-parameter and Hom-quotient comparisons are recorded gaps.
acceptance: The regular-local-ring facts used (A/p₁ regular of dimension n − 1; a one-dimensional regular local ring is a discrete valuation ring) are standard inputs; for Λ = O⟦T⟧ they are explicit (A/ϖ = k⟦T⟧).

sources.match: Proposition 5.1.9 and its proof (after Diekert).

nodes.title: Structure theorem over a two-dimensional regular local ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a two-dimensional regular local ring and M a finitely generated A-module. There are finitely many height-one primes 𝔭_i, an integer r ≥ 0, integers n_i ≥ 1 and a pseudo-isomorphism M → A^r ⊕ ⊕_i A/𝔭_i^{n_i}. The data are determined by M: r = dim_K M ⊗_A K, {𝔭_i} = supp(T_A(M)) ∩ P(A), and the n_i are unique (Theorem 5.1.10).
hypotheses: A two-dimensional regular local ring, integrally closed (see reflexive-free-over-regular-local).
proofSteps: Proposition 5.1.7(i) splits M up to pseudo-isomorphism as T_A(M) ⊕ F_A(M).
Proposition 5.1.8 embeds F_A(M) into its reflexive hull by an injective pseudo-isomorphism, and the hull is free by Proposition 5.1.9.
Proposition 5.1.7(ii) treats T_A(M); uniqueness from 5.1.7 and r = dim_K M ⊗ K.
acceptance: For A = Λ = O⟦T⟧ this is the input to the structure theorem for Iwasawa modules.
For M=A the elementary family is empty and r=1; it is the support of T_A(M), not all of M, that indexes its height-one primes (E16).

nodes.title: O⟦T⟧ is a two-dimensional regular local ring
nodes.statement: For a complete DVR O, O[[T]] is a regular local ring of dimension two.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Reuse pinned noetherianity, factoriality and the constant-term unit criterion. Prove the dimension upper bound and independent residue classes of ϖ,T; these are recorded proof inputs, not consequences of merely naming IsRegularLocalRing.
acceptance: The dimension formula dim R⟦X⟧ = dim R + 1 is a cited commutative-algebra input.

nodes.title: The height-one primes of O⟦T⟧
nodes.statement: Every height-one prime of O[[T]] is (ϖ) or (F), with F an irreducible distinguished polynomial.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: In the UFD it is generated by an irreducible. If this is not associated to ϖ it has finite reduced degree; preparation produces F, and irreducibility descends through the unit factor.
acceptance: NSW proves the case O = ℤ_p; the argument uses only factoriality and preparation, so it holds verbatim with ϖ in place of p.

nodes.title: Mathlib's Weierstrass theory as NSW's division lemma and preparation theorem
nodes.statement: For a monic polynomial F over a commutative ring O, multiplication by the native AdjoinRoot.root F has characteristic polynomial F in the native monic power basis, including F=1. For a complete local coefficient ring and a series f with finite reduced degree, transport this identity through the pinned Weierstrass quotient equivalence to identify multiplication by T on O[[T]]/(f) with its distinguished factor.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
NSW allows any complete noetherian local O with finite residue field; Mathlib needs IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal O) O.
proofSteps: Use AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' for monic F. Compute multiplication by the root on the basis: shift the lower basis vectors and use the monic relation on the last one.

Compute the characteristic polynomial of that companion matrix directly over O; for degree zero the empty determinant is one. This route does not apply the field-only AdjoinRoot.minpoly_root to a DVR.
Transport across the pinned Weierstrass quotient algebra equivalence. The companion determinant calculation and transport remain proof obligations.
acceptance: The proposed monic-root signature is valid over any commutative ring and its F=1 example uses the actual rank-zero quotient. The series quotient transport is still a separate interface gap.

nodes.title: Structure theorem for Iwasawa modules
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated module over Λ = O⟦T⟧. There are r ≥ 0, integers m_i ≥ 1, irreducible distinguished polynomials F_j and integers n_j ≥ 1, and a homomorphism M → E = Λ^r ⊕ ⊕_i Λ/(ϖ^{m_i}) ⊕ ⊕_j Λ/(F_j^{n_j}) with finite kernel and cokernel. The number r, the multisets (m_i) and (n_j) and the ideals (F_j) are determined by M (Theorem 5.3.8 for O = ℤ_p). The μ-part is built from powers of the uniformizer ϖ, not of p: RJW Theorem 13.1 writes Λ/(p^{n_i}) over O_L⟦T⟧, which fails when L/ℚ_p is ramified (source finding E15).
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Apply structure-theorem-regular-dimension-two to Λ, which is a two-dimensional regular local ring (iwasawa-algebra-regular-local).
The height-one primes are (ϖ) and (F) (height-one-primes); both are principal, so 𝔭^n = (ϖ^n) or (F^n).
Over Λ pseudo-null means finite (pseudo-null, Remark 4), so the pseudo-isomorphism has finite kernel and cokernel.
Uniqueness comes from the elementary-divisor multisets in the structure theorem after localisation at each height-one DVR. Total length alone does not distinguish Λ/(T²) from Λ/(T) ⊕ Λ/(T).
acceptance: For O ramified over ℤ_p with index e, Λ/(ϖ) is not pseudo-isomorphic to any Λ^r ⊕ ⊕Λ/(p^{n_i}) ⊕ ⊕Λ/(F_j^{m_j}): its length at (ϖ) is 1, while Λ/(p^n) = Λ/(ϖ^{en}) has length en there and Λ/(F^m) has length 0.

nodes.title: Iwasawa invariants and the characteristic polynomial
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated Λ-module M define μ(M) as the finite length, over Λ_(ϖ), of the localisation of T_Λ(M) at (ϖ). For torsion M this is length M_(ϖ); on arbitrary M the torsion submodule is essential.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Use the finite elementary decomposition of the torsion submodule. Its vertical exponents sum to this finite local length; all horizontal and pseudo-null terms vanish at (ϖ).
acceptance: μ is normalised by v_ϖ; the class-number normalisation is O = ℤ_p, where μ is Iwasawa's μ.

nodes.title: The characteristic ideal
nodes.statement: For a finite torsion module over a noetherian normal UFD A, define charIdeal(M) as the finite product of the height-one prime ideals raised to their local-length multiplicities in charDivisor(M). This is an actual native ideal; unique factorisation makes it principal.
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
Λ, O as in the structure theorem for the comparison.
M is a finitely generated torsion module over the indicated ring; exact sequences in this statement consist of such modules.
proofSteps: Use the native finitely supported characteristic divisor. Take its product in Ideal A, with each prime ideal raised to the assigned multiplicity.

Prove finite height-one support and finite local lengths before interpreting those natural-number multiplicities; conversion from extended length is not a proof of finiteness. The cyclic, exactness and transport APIs follow from local length calculations.
acceptance: The intrinsic length definition, the functoriality and the norm formula are worker derivations: NSW define only F_{M,γ} and RJW define Ch_Λ through the structure theorem.

nodes.title: Iwasawa's growth formula
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated torsion Λ-module and n₀ ≥ d(M). Then #(M/(ω_n/ω_{n₀})M) = p^{μp^n + λn + ν} for all sufficiently large n, where μ = μ(M), λ = λ(M) and ν does not depend on n (Proposition 5.3.17). Its separate proof input is cyclotomic-growth-step (Lemma5.3.18). When d(M) = −1, taking n₀ = −1 (ω_{−1} = 1) gives #M_{Γ_n} = #M/ω_nM = p^{μp^n+λn+ν}.
hypotheses: Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ for Γ ≅ ℤ_p with a chosen topological generator γ, T = γ − 1; Γ_n is the subgroup of index p^n, ω_n = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1 and ξ_n = ω_n/ω_{n−1} (ω_{−1} = 1).
proofSteps: ν_n = ω_n/ω_{n₀} is prime to supp(M) ∩ P(Λ) for n ≥ n₀, so multiplication by ν_n is a pseudo-isomorphism (Lemma 5.1.6) and M/ν_nM is finite.
ν_n is injective on M/M₀, so #M/ν_n = #(M/M₀)/ν_n · #M₀/ν_n, and the second factor is eventually constant.
For N = M/M₀ ⊆ E (elementary, finite cokernel C), #N/ν_n = #E/ν_n by the snake lemma.
#(Λ/p^m)/ν_n = p^{m(p^n − deg ω_(n₀))}; where deg ω_(−1)=0 and deg ω_(n₀)=p^{n₀} for n₀≥0; for E_j = Λ/F_j^{n_j}, Lemma 5.3.18 gives #E_j/ν_{n+1} = p^{n_j deg F_j}·#E_j/ν_n for n ≫ 0.

Lemma 5.3.18: T is nilpotent on M/pM, so γ lies in a p-Sylow subgroup of GL(λ, 𝔽_p) and γ^{p^m} = 1 on M/pM for m ≥ λ(λ − 1)/2; for n > λ(λ − 1)/2, A^{p^n} ≡ I mod p², so Σ_{k<p}A^{p^nk} = pU with U invertible.
acceptance: Stated for O = ℤ_p, the class-number normalisation the stage asks for.
Lemma 5.3.18 is checked for λ = 1, p = 3 in the suggested file.

Evaluation of the group ring at characters and the joint evaluation
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring O, a commutative group G and a character ψ : G → O^× (a group homomorphism), the character evaluation ev_ψ : O[G] → O is the O-algebra homomorphism Σ_g a_g g ↦ Σ_g a_g ψ(g), the lift of g ↦ ψ(g) through the universal property of the monoid algebra; it is the Tau Ceti declaration TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point ψ with value algebra A = O and is not defined again; TauCeti.charEval is an abbreviation for it. For a set Ψ of characters the joint evaluation ev_Ψ : O[G] → ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O is x ↦ (ev_ψ(x))_{ψ∈Ψ}; this is the new construction. Following Dasgupta–Kakde, ψ(x) means ev_ψ(x) for x ∈ O[G].
hypotheses: O is a commutative ring and G a commutative group; the maps need no finiteness. Row orthogonality assumes G finite and O a domain.
A character is a group homomorphism ψ : G → O^×; the trivial character is 1.
Injectivity of the joint evaluation at all characters is a separate lemma (API item TauCeti.jointEval_injective); it assumes G finite and O a domain with HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G).
proofSteps: ev_ψ is TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point ψ for R = A = O, that is MonoidAlgebra.lift O O G applied to the composite of ψ with the inclusion O^× → O (Units.coeHom); point_single gives ev_ψ(a·g) = a·ψ(g), and point_single_one or MonoidAlgebra.lift_of gives ev_ψ(g) = ψ(g).
The joint evaluation is AlgHom.pi of the family (ev_ψ)_{ψ∈Ψ}.

Row orthogonality: for G finite, O a domain and ψ ≠ 1, Σ_g ψ(g) = 0 by sum_hom_units_eq_zero applied to the composite of ψ with Units.coeHom, which is not the trivial homomorphism G → O because Units.coeHom is injective.
ev_1 is the coefficient sum: on a·g both ev_1 and TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.augmentation O G take the value a (point_single, augmentation_single), and both are additive.

On the one-dimensional representation Representation.ofLinearCharacter ψ, which is the source's O_ψ, the action of O[G] through Representation.asAlgebraHom is the lift of g ↦ (multiplication by ψ(g)); it and x ↦ (multiplication by ev_ψ(x)) are O-algebra homomorphisms O[G] → End_O(O) that agree on group elements, hence are equal.
acceptance: ev_ψ(g) = ψ(g); ev_1 is the augmentation.
For G of order 2 with generator h and ψ(h) = −1: ev_ψ(1 + h) = 0 and ev_ψ(1 − h) = 2.
G = C_2 = {1, h} and O a domain of characteristic ≠ 2: the characters of C_2 are 1 and the sign h ↦ −1, and the joint evaluation at these two sends a + bh to (a + b, a − b).

nodes.title: The joint evaluation at all characters is injective
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite commutative group and O a domain with HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G). Then the joint evaluation ev_Ĝ : O[G] → ∏_{ψ∈Ĝ} O at all characters ψ : G → O^× is injective: if ψ(x) = 0 for every character ψ, then x = 0.
hypotheses: G is a finite commutative group and O is a domain with enough roots of unity for the exponent of G (HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G)). This holds in the Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2), where O is the valuation ring of a finite extension of Q_p containing all values of all characters of G.

No hypothesis #G ≠ 0 is needed: it follows from the two above. A domain containing a primitive e-th root of unity, e = Monoid.exponent G, has e ≠ 0 in it (IsPrimitiveRoot.neZero'), and #G divides a power of e (card_dvd_exponent_pow_rank).
The product and the sum over characters are indexed by the finite type Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×) (instFintypeMonoidHomUnits).
proofSteps: For x = Σ_h a_h h and g ∈ G, Σ_{ψ∈Ĝ} ψ(g)^{-1} ev_ψ(x) = Σ_h a_h Σ_{ψ∈Ĝ} ψ(g)^{-1}ψ(h), because ev_ψ(x) = Σ_h a_h ψ(h) (character-evaluation, TauCeti.charEval_single) and the two finite sums can be exchanged.
By the column orthogonality CommGroup.sum_inv_mul_monoidHom_apply_eq_ite the inner sum over ψ : G →* O^× is #G if h = g and 0 otherwise. Hence Σ_{ψ∈Ĝ} ψ(g)^{-1} ev_ψ(x) = #G·a_g.

#G ≠ 0 in O. The exponent e = Monoid.exponent G is positive because G is finite (Monoid.exponent_ne_zero_of_finite), and O contains a primitive e-th root of unity (the field prim of HasEnoughRootsOfUnity), so e ≠ 0 in the domain O (IsPrimitiveRoot.neZero'). Moreover #G divides e^r, where r is the minimal number of generators of G (card_dvd_exponent_pow_rank); e^r ≠ 0 in the domain O, and a divisor of a nonzero element is nonzero.
If ev_ψ(x) = 0 for all ψ, then #G·a_g = 0 for every g, so a_g = 0 because #G ≠ 0 in the domain O by the previous step; thus x = 0.
acceptance: G = C_2 = {1, h}, O = Z_3: the characters are 1 and the sign, and a + bh ↦ (a + b, a − b) is injective because 2 ≠ 0.
The roots of unity are needed: for O = Z_5 and G = C_3 the only character is trivial, and ev_1 kills g − 1.
O must be a domain: for O = Z/4 and G = C_2 there are two characters and 2 ≠ 0 in O, but 2 + 2h ↦ (0, 0).

In characteristic ℓ the hypothesis on roots of unity excludes ℓ | #G: for O = F_3[t] and G = C_3, x³ − 1 = (x − 1)³ has no root of order 3, HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O 3 fails, the only character is trivial and ev_1 kills g − 1.

nodes.title: Character group rings
nodes.statement: In the Dasgupta–Kakde setting, for a subset Ψ ⊆ Ĝ the character group ring R_Ψ is the image of the joint evaluation ev_Ψ : O[G] → ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O, an O-subalgebra of the product, together with the canonical surjection α_Ψ : O[G] ↠ R_Ψ; equivalently R_Ψ = O[G]/⋂_{ψ∈Ψ} ker ev_ψ. Quotients of O[G] of this form are the character group rings. R_Ψ is in general a proper, non-maximal O-order in ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O and is never replaced by that product; it is not Gorenstein in general.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
Ψ ⊆ Ĝ is arbitrary: Ψ = ∅ gives the zero ring, Ψ = {1} gives O through the augmentation, Ψ = Ĝ gives O[G].
No Gorenstein property is part of the definition. L6's Gorenstein-order and exact-duality results apply to an R_Ψ only after it has been proved Gorenstein (test charGroupRing_not_gorenstein).

R_Ψ, α_Ψ, the evaluations, the restriction maps and the items R_∅ = 0 and R_{1} ≅ O make sense for every commutative ring O, every commutative group G and every set Ψ of characters; the items that need G finite or O a domain say so.
proofSteps: Define R_Ψ as AlgHom.range of ev_Ψ and α_Ψ as AlgHom.rangeRestrict; α_Ψ is surjective by AlgHom.rangeRestrict_surjective.
ker α_Ψ = ⋂_{ψ∈Ψ} ker ev_ψ because R_Ψ sits inside the product and its ψ-coordinate of α_Ψ(x) is ψ(x).
For Ψ ⊆ Ψ′, restriction of coordinates ∏_{Ψ′} O → ∏_Ψ O maps R_{Ψ′} onto R_Ψ compatibly with α; functoriality is coordinate restriction.
For ψ ∈ Ψ the coordinate projection ∏_{ψ′∈Ψ} O → O at ψ restricts to an O-algebra homomorphism ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O with ev_ψ ∘ α_Ψ = ev_ψ on O[G]; it is surjective because it is O-linear and sends 1 to 1.
An O-algebra homomorphism on O[G] that vanishes on ker α_Ψ factors uniquely through the surjection α_Ψ, and O[G]/ker α_Ψ ≅ R_Ψ is Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective applied to α_Ψ.
If Ψ = Ψ₁ ∪ Ψ₂, an element of R_Ψ whose restrictions to Ψ₁ and to Ψ₂ vanish has all coordinates zero, so it is zero; hence R_Ψ → R_{Ψ₁} × R_{Ψ₂} is injective.

For Ψ = Ĝ, G finite and O a domain with HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G), α_Ĝ is injective by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/joint-evaluation-injective and surjective by construction: O[G] ≅ R_Ĝ.
acceptance: α_Ĝ : O[G] → R_Ĝ is an isomorphism (API item equivGroupRing, from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/joint-evaluation-injective).
For Ψ_χ = {ψ : ψ|_{G′} = χ}, R_{Ψ_χ} is the connected component R_χ = O[G_p]_χ of O[G]; this is proved in the nodes on the components of O[G].

nodes.title: #G times each coordinate idempotent lies in a character group ring
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite commutative group, O a domain and Ψ a set of characters G → O^×. For ψ ∈ Ψ, α_Ψ(Σ_{g∈G} ψ(g)^{-1} g) = #G·δ_ψ, the vector of ∏_{ψ′∈Ψ} O with #G at ψ and 0 elsewhere. Hence #G·∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O ⊆ R_Ψ ⊆ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O.
hypotheses: G is a finite commutative group and O is a domain; no hypothesis on roots of unity is needed. Ψ is finite, because a finite group has finitely many homomorphisms to the units of a domain (instFintypeMonoidHomUnits).
The statement fails for rings with zero divisors: for O = Z/8 and G = C_2, which has four characters, 2·δ_1 is not in R_Ĝ.
proofSteps: The ψ′-coordinate of α_Ψ(Σ_g ψ(g)^{-1} g) is Σ_g (ψ^{-1}ψ′)(g) (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.coord_proj; character-evaluation, TauCeti.charEval_of).
For ψ′ ≠ ψ the character ψ^{-1}ψ′ is not trivial and the sum is 0 by row orthogonality (character-evaluation, TauCeti.charEval_sum_eq_zero, that is sum_hom_units_eq_zero); for ψ′ = ψ it is #G.
R_Ψ is an O-submodule of the product, and the vectors δ_ψ, ψ ∈ Ψ, span the product over O because Ψ is finite; so #G·∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O ⊆ R_Ψ.
acceptance: If #G is a unit of O, then R_Ψ = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O for every Ψ; in the Dasgupta–Kakde setting this is the case p ∤ #G.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.5, arXiv v3 PDF p. 17
sources.match: The source asserts without proof that R_Ψ has finite index in O_Ψ = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O; this lemma is the explicit inclusion #G·O_Ψ ⊆ R_Ψ behind that assertion.

nodes.title: Character group rings are free O-modules of rank #Ψ
nodes.statement: In the Dasgupta–Kakde setting, for Ψ ⊆ Ĝ the character group ring R_Ψ is a free O-module of rank #Ψ: it is a full-rank O-lattice in ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
What is used: O is a principal ideal domain (for freeness, as proved here), G is finite and #G ≠ 0 in O (for the rank). No hypothesis on roots of unity or on the residue field is needed.
proofSteps: R_Ψ is an O-submodule of the finite free module O^Ψ. A submodule of a finite free module over a principal ideal domain is free: Submodule.smithNormalForm gives a basis of the submodule.

By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-scaled-idempotent, #G·O^Ψ ⊆ R_Ψ ⊆ O^Ψ. The inclusion R_Ψ → O^Ψ and the map O^Ψ → R_Ψ, v ↦ #G·v, are injective O-linear maps between finite O-modules (the second because #G ≠ 0 in the domain O), so rank R_Ψ ≤ rank O^Ψ ≤ rank R_Ψ (LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective, twice), and rank O^Ψ = #Ψ (Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card).
acceptance: If p ∤ #G then #G ∈ O^× and R_Ψ = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O for every Ψ.
G = C_p, O = Z_p[ζ_p], Ψ = Ĝ: R_Ĝ ≅ O[C_p] is free of rank p, with basis the images of 1, g, …, g^{p−1}.
Ψ = ∅: R_∅ = 0 is free of rank 0.

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source states only that R_Ψ is a finite-index subring of a finite product of DVRs; freeness of rank #Ψ is the lattice form of that statement and is proved here.

nodes.title: Character group rings have finite index in the product
nodes.statement: In the Dasgupta–Kakde setting, for Ψ ⊆ Ĝ the quotient O-module (∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O)/R_Ψ is finite: R_Ψ is a subring of finite index of a finite product of copies of the discrete valuation ring O. More precisely, the quotient is a quotient of (O/#G)^Ψ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).

What is used: G is finite, O is a domain, and O/(#G) is finite. The last holds when #G ≠ 0 in O and O has finite quotients (Ring.HasFiniteQuotients O), in particular for a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field in which #G ≠ 0.

A local domain of characteristic zero with finite residue field is not enough: for O = Z_p[ζ_p]⟦T⟧, G = C_p and Ψ = {1, ψ}, R_Ψ = {(a, b) : a ≡ b mod (ζ_p − 1)} and (O × O)/R_Ψ ≅ O/(ζ_p − 1) = F_p⟦T⟧ is infinite.
proofSteps: By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-scaled-idempotent, #G·O^Ψ ⊆ R_Ψ, so O^Ψ/R_Ψ is a quotient of O^Ψ/#G·O^Ψ = (O/#G)^Ψ.

O/(#G) is finite: #G ≠ 0 in the characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring O, so (#G) = (ϖ^n) = 𝔪_O^n for a uniformiser ϖ and some n (IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_irreducible, IsDiscreteValuationRing.ideal_eq_span_pow_irreducible, Irreducible.maximalIdeal_eq), and O/𝔪_O^n is finite because the residue field is finite and 𝔪_O = (ϖ) is finitely generated (Ideal.finite_quotient_pow). Ψ is finite, so (O/#G)^Ψ is finite.
acceptance: G = C_p, O = Z_p[ζ_p], Ψ = Ĝ: #(∏_ψ O / O[C_p]) = p^{p(p−1)/2}, the norm of the Vandermonde determinant ∏_{i<j}(ζ^j − ζ^i), whose square is ±p^p; for p = 3 the index is 27.
G = C_p, O = Z_p[ζ_p], Ψ = {1, ψ}: (O × O)/R_Ψ ≅ O/(ζ_p − 1) has p elements.
If p ∤ #G the quotient is zero.

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source asserts the finite index without proof; the proof here rests on the explicit inclusion #G·∏O ⊆ R_Ψ.

nodes.title: Non-zerodivisors of a character group ring
nodes.statement: For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ and x ∈ R_Ψ the following are equivalent: x is a non-zerodivisor of R_Ψ; ψ(x) ≠ 0 for every ψ ∈ Ψ; x is a non-zerodivisor of ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O. Multiplication by such x is injective on ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O, so it induces an isomorphism of O-modules (∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O)/R_Ψ → x(∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O)/xR_Ψ, as used in Lemma 2.5.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
What is used: G is finite and O is a domain with #G ≠ 0.
proofSteps: If ψ(x) = 0 for some ψ ∈ Ψ, then y = #G·δ_ψ lies in R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-scaled-idempotent), is nonzero because #G ≠ 0 in O, and xy = 0.
If every ψ(x) ≠ 0, x is a non-zerodivisor of the product of copies of the domain O, hence of its subring R_Ψ.

An element of a product of copies of a domain is a non-zerodivisor exactly when all its coordinates are nonzero; this gives the third condition, and injectivity of multiplication by x on the product gives the isomorphism (∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O)/R_Ψ → x(∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O)/xR_Ψ.
acceptance: For G of order 2, O = Z_3 and Ψ = Ĝ, x = 1 + h is a zerodivisor (ψ(x) = 0 for the sign character) while x = 3 + h is not.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.5, arXiv v3 PDF p. 17
sources.match: The source uses that x is a non-zerodivisor of the product O_Ψ; this lemma supplies it from x being one in R_Ψ (the unproved step recorded as PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E18 for Lemma 2.4).

nodes.title: Quotients by subgroup norms are character group rings
nodes.statement: (Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 2.2.) Let I ⊆ G be a subgroup and N_I = Σ_{σ∈I} σ ∈ O[G], the element TauCeti.subgroupCharSum of the trivial character over I. For Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ(I) ≠ 1}, the kernel of α_Ψ : O[G] ↠ R_Ψ is exactly the principal ideal N_I·O[G]; hence O[G]/N_I ≅ R_Ψ is a character group ring.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
ψ(I) ≠ 1 means that ψ is not trivial on I. What is used: G is finite and O is a domain with HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G), through the injectivity of the joint evaluation.
proofSteps: ψ(N_I) = Σ_{σ∈I} ψ(σ) = 0 when ψ|_I ≠ 1, by row orthogonality on the finite group I (sum_hom_units_eq_zero applied to the restriction of ψ to I composed with Units.coeHom); so N_I ∈ ker α_Ψ.
If α_Ψ(x) = 0 and g ∈ I, then ψ(gx) = ψ(g)ψ(x) equals ψ(x) for every ψ ∈ Ĝ: trivially when ψ(g) = 1, and because ψ ∈ Ψ and ψ(x) = 0 otherwise.

Injectivity of the joint evaluation at all characters (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/joint-evaluation-injective) gives gx = x for all g ∈ I. For x = N_I itself this invariance is TauCeti.single_mul_subgroupCharSum with the trivial character.
An I-invariant x = Σ a_h h has coefficients constant on I-cosets; choosing coset representatives h_j gives x = N_I·Σ_j a_{h_j} h_j.
acceptance: I = G: O[G]/N_G ≅ R_{Ĝ∖{1}}; for G = C_p this is O[x]/(1 + x + … + x^{p−1}).

sources.locator: Lemma 2.2 and proof, arXiv v3 PDF p. 16
sources.match: Lemma 2.2 with its proof; the injectivity of O[G] → ∏_{Ĝ} O_ψ that the proof uses is the lemma on the joint evaluation at all characters.

nodes.title: Values of the characters of G on the idempotent e_χ
nodes.statement: Write G = G_p × G′ and let χ ∈ Ĝ′, with idempotent e_χ = (#G′)^{-1} Σ_{a∈G′} χ(a)^{-1} a ∈ O[G′] ⊆ O[G], the character idempotent of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition for H = G′ transported along O[G′] → O[G]. For every character ψ ∈ Ĝ: ψ(e_χ) = 1 if ψ|_{G′} = χ, and ψ(e_χ) = 0 otherwise.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).

#G′ is a unit of O because p ∤ #G′. The idempotent e_χ is that of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition, which is stated for O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field of characteristic p and a finite abelian group H with p ∤ #H; both hold here for H = G′.
What is used: O is a domain and G′ is a finite subgroup of the commutative group G whose order is a unit of O. Neither the complement G_p nor a hypothesis on roots of unity is used.
proofSteps: The inclusion G′ → G induces the O-algebra homomorphism O[G′] → O[G] (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom). For a ∈ G′ the value of ev_ψ on the image of a is ψ(a) (character-evaluation, TauCeti.charEval_of), so ψ(e_χ) = (#G′)^{-1} Σ_{a∈G′} χ(a)^{-1}ψ(a) = (#G′)^{-1} Σ_{a∈G′} (χ^{-1}·ψ|_{G′})(a).
If ψ|_{G′} = χ every term is 1, the sum is #G′ and ψ(e_χ) = 1.
Otherwise χ^{-1}·ψ|_{G′} is a nontrivial character of the finite group G′, and the sum is 0 by row orthogonality in the domain O (sum_hom_units_eq_zero applied to its composite with Units.coeHom).
acceptance: G′ = C_2 = {1, h}, p odd, χ the sign character: e_χ = (1 − h)/2 and ψ(e_χ) = (1 − ψ(h))/2, which is 1 if ψ(h) = −1 and 0 if ψ(h) = 1.
G′ trivial (G = G_p): e_1 = 1 and ψ(e_1) = 1 for every ψ.
For every ψ ∈ Ĝ exactly one χ ∈ Ĝ′ has ψ(e_χ) = 1, in agreement with Σ_χ e_χ = 1 and e_χe_ω = 0 for χ ≠ ω.

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source names the characters belonging to χ and asserts that the component R_χ is their character group ring; it does not state this evaluation, which is the computation behind that assertion.

nodes.title: The kernel of the projection to the characters belonging to χ
nodes.statement: Write G = G_p × G′. For χ ∈ Ĝ′ = Hom(G′, O^×) let e_χ = (#G′)^{-1} Σ_{a∈G′} χ(a)^{-1} a ∈ O[G′] ⊆ O[G] be its idempotent, the character idempotent of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition for H = G′ transported along O[G′] → O[G], and let Ψ_χ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ} be the set of characters belonging to χ. Then ker α_{Ψ_χ} = (1 − e_χ)O[G]; the reason is that ψ(e_χ) = 1 for ψ ∈ Ψ_χ and ψ(e_χ) = 0 for ψ ∈ Ĝ ∖ Ψ_χ. Hence R_{Ψ_χ} ≅ O[G]/(1 − e_χ) ≅ e_χO[G] =: R_χ, the connected component of O[G] attached to χ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
#G′ is a unit of O because p ∤ #G′, and O contains the values of χ because the exponent of G′ divides that of G.

The idempotents e_ω and their relations are those of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition and its relation lemmas, which are stated for O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field of characteristic p and a finite abelian group H with p ∤ #H; both hold here for H = G′.
The kernel statement holds for every subgroup G′ of G whose order is a unit of O; the complement G_p plays no part in it.
proofSteps: Transport: the inclusion G′ → G induces the O-algebra homomorphism O[G′] → O[G] (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom), and e_χ ∈ O[G] is the image of the L4 idempotent of χ. In O[G′], #G′·e_χ is TauCeti.subgroupCharSum of the character χ^{-1} over the whole group G′.
For ψ ∈ Ĝ, ψ(e_χ) is 1 if ψ|_{G′} = χ and 0 otherwise (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-idempotent-evaluation). Hence 1 − e_χ ∈ ker α_{Ψ_χ}.

If x ∈ ker α_{Ψ_χ}, then ψ(e_χx) = ψ(e_χ)ψ(x) = 0 for all ψ ∈ Ĝ: it is zero on Ψ_χ by hypothesis and zero off Ψ_χ by the previous step. So e_χx = 0 by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/joint-evaluation-injective, and x = (1 − e_χ)x.
e_χ is idempotent in O[G′] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition-api-1), hence in O[G]; so O[G]/(1 − e_χ) ≅ e_χO[G] by x ↦ e_χx.
acceptance: G = G′ (p ∤ #G): Ψ_χ = {χ} and R_{Ψ_χ} ≅ O for every χ.
G = G_p: there is one component, χ = 1, e_1 = 1 and ker α_Ĝ = 0.
G′ = C_2 = {1, h}, p odd, χ the sign character: e_χ = (1 − h)/2, and ψ(e_χ) = (1 − ψ(h))/2 is 1 or 0 according to ψ(h) = −1 or ψ(h) = 1.

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source states that the component R_χ is the character group ring of Ψ_χ and gives no proof; the steps above prove it in the form ker α_{Ψ_χ} = (1 − e_χ)O[G].

nodes.title: The component R_χ is the twisted group ring O[G_p]_χ
nodes.statement: Write G = G_p × G′ and let χ ∈ Ĝ′. The O-algebra homomorphism π_χ : O[G] → O[G_p], g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)g_p for g′ ∈ G′ and g_p ∈ G_p, is surjective with kernel (1 − e_χ)O[G] = ker α_{Ψ_χ}. Hence there is a unique isomorphism of O-algebras R_{Ψ_χ} → O[G_p] sending α_{Ψ_χ}(g′g_p) to χ(g′)g_p. With G acting on O[G_p] through π_χ this is the source's O[G_p]_χ, so R_χ ≅ O[G_p]_χ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
#G′ is a unit of O. The statement holds for every decomposition G = G_p × G′ into complementary subgroups with #G′ a unit of O; that G_p is the p-Sylow subgroup is not used.

The idempotents e_ω and their relations are those of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition and its relation lemmas, which are stated for O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field of characteristic p and a finite abelian group H with p ∤ #H; both hold here for H = G′.
proofSteps: π_χ is the lift (MonoidAlgebra.lift) of the monoid homomorphism G → O[G_p], g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)·g_p; it is surjective because it restricts to the identity on G_p.

g′·e_χ = χ(g′)·e_χ in O[G] for g′ ∈ G′. In O[G′], #G′·e_χ is TauCeti.subgroupCharSum of the character χ^{-1} over the whole group, and TauCeti.single_mul_subgroupCharSum gives g′·(#G′·e_χ) = χ^{-1}(g′^{-1})·(#G′·e_χ) = χ(g′)·(#G′·e_χ); divide by the unit #G′ and apply O[G′] → O[G] (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom). This identity is not among the L4 relations.

π_χ(e_χ) = (#G′)^{-1} Σ_a χ(a)^{-1}χ(a) = 1, so 1 − e_χ ∈ ker π_χ. Conversely, by the previous step e_χ·g′g_p = χ(g′)·e_χ g_p, so every element of e_χO[G] is e_χ·y with y ∈ O[G_p], and π_χ(e_χ y) = y; hence π_χ is injective on e_χO[G] and ker π_χ = (1 − e_χ)O[G].

By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/component-character-group-ring, (1 − e_χ)O[G] = ker α_{Ψ_χ}. Two surjective O-algebra homomorphisms from O[G] with the same kernel induce an isomorphism of their targets (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.lift), unique because α_{Ψ_χ} is surjective.
acceptance: G = G′ (p ∤ #G): R_{Ψ_χ} ≅ O, with α(g′) ↦ χ(g′).
G = G_p: χ = 1 and the isomorphism is the inverse of α_Ĝ : O[G_p] → R_Ĝ.
For ψ = χ·ψ_p ∈ Ψ_χ with ψ_p a character of G_p, the evaluation ev_ψ on R_{Ψ_χ} corresponds to ev_{ψ_p} on O[G_p]; so #Ψ_χ = #G_p, the rank of O[G_p].

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source defines O[G_p]_χ (in its formula χ(g) is χ of the G′-component of g and the second g is the image of g in G_p) and identifies it with the component R_χ without proof; the steps above construct the isomorphism.

uses.where: Dasgupta–Kakde §2.2 (PDF p. 15) and the preamble of §5 (PDF p. 31), R = O[G_p]_χ
uses.how: identifies the ring O[G_p]_χ in which the paper works with the character group ring R_{Ψ_χ}, to which the results on character group rings apply
the trivial-zero-free ring R_Ψ, Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ, is introduced as a quotient of the component O[G_p]_χ
the Fitting-ideal statements of the Brumer–Stark argument are made over a component O[G_p]_χ

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentProj
api.statement: π_χ : O[G] →ₐ[O] O[G_p], the lift (MonoidAlgebra.lift) of the monoid homomorphism G → O[G_p], g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)·g_p for g′ ∈ G′ and g_p ∈ G_p.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentProj_single
api.statement: π_χ(a·g′g_p) = aχ(g′)·g_p for a ∈ O, g′ ∈ G′, g_p ∈ G_p.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentProj_surjective
api.statement: π_χ is surjective; it restricts to the identity on O[G_p] ⊆ O[G].

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentProj_charIdempotent
api.statement: π_χ(e_χ) = 1, and π_χ(e_ω) = 0 for ω ∈ Ĝ′ with ω ≠ χ.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.ker_componentProj
api.statement: ker π_χ = (1 − e_χ)O[G] = ker α_{Ψ_χ}.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv
api.statement: R_{Ψ_χ} ≃ₐ[O] O[G_p], induced by the two surjections α_{Ψ_χ} and π_χ from O[G], which have the same kernel.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_proj
api.statement: componentEquiv(α_{Ψ_χ}(x)) = π_χ(x) for x ∈ O[G]; in particular α_{Ψ_χ}(g′g_p) ↦ χ(g′)·g_p.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_symm_of
api.statement: The inverse of componentEquiv sends g_p ∈ G_p to α_{Ψ_χ}(g_p).

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_unique
api.statement: An O-algebra homomorphism f : R_{Ψ_χ} → O[G_p] with f(α_{Ψ_χ}(g′g_p)) = χ(g′)·g_p for all g′ ∈ G′ and g_p ∈ G_p is equal to componentEquiv.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.charEval_componentEquiv
api.statement: For a character ψ_p of G_p and ψ = (g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)ψ_p(g_p)) ∈ Ψ_χ: ev_{ψ_p}(componentEquiv(y)) = ev_ψ(y) for y ∈ R_{Ψ_χ}, where ev_ψ is TauCeti.charGroupRing.eval and ev_{ψ_p} is the character evaluation on O[G_p].

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_of_trivial_complement
api.statement: G′ trivial (G′ = 1, G_p = G, χ = 1): under the identification O[G] ≅ O[G_p] induced by G ≅ G_p, π_1 is that identification, and componentEquiv composed with the restriction R_Ĝ → R_{Ψ_1} (Ψ_1 is the set of all characters) and with TauCeti.charGroupRing.equivGroupRing is that identification.

api.name: TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_of_trivial_sylow
api.statement: G_p trivial (G′ = G, G_p = 1): Ψ_χ = {χ}, π_χ(x) = ev_χ(x)·1 in O[G_p], which is O through its structure map, and componentEquiv(α_{Ψ_χ}(g′)) = χ(g′)·1.

tests.name: componentProj_sign
tests.statement: G′ = C_2 = {1, h}, p odd, χ the sign character: π_χ(h·g_p) = −g_p for g_p ∈ G_p, π_χ((1 − h)/2) = 1 and π_χ((1 + h)/2) = 0.

tests.name: componentEquiv_trivialComplement
tests.statement: G′ trivial (G′ = 1, G_p = G, χ = 1): componentEquiv applied to the restriction of α_Ĝ(x) to R_{Ψ_1} is the image of x under the identification O[G] ≅ O[G_p], for every x ∈ O[G].

tests.name: componentEquiv_trivialSylow
tests.statement: G_p trivial (G′ = G, G_p = 1): componentEquiv(α_{Ψ_χ}(g′)) = χ(g′)·1 in O[G_p], which is O through its structure map.

tests.name: componentProj_eval
tests.statement: For a character ψ_p of G_p and ψ = (g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)ψ_p(g_p)): ev_{ψ_p}(π_χ(x)) = ev_ψ(x) for every x ∈ O[G].

tests.name: componentProj_twist
tests.statement: The twist is by χ and not by χ^{-1}: if χ² ≠ 1 then π_{χ^{-1}}(e_χ) = 0, whereas π_χ(e_χ) = 1. And π_χ is not injective when G′ ≠ 1: it kills 1 − e_χ ≠ 0.

nodes.title: O[G] is the product of its components R_χ
nodes.statement: Write G = G_p × G′. The idempotents e_χ ∈ O[G], χ ∈ Ĝ′, are pairwise orthogonal with sum 1, and the O-algebra homomorphism O[G] → ∏_{χ∈Ĝ′} R_{Ψ_χ}, x ↦ (α_{Ψ_χ}(x))_χ, is an isomorphism. The sets Ψ_χ, χ ∈ Ĝ′, partition Ĝ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
#G′ is a unit of O, and O contains the values of the characters of G′ because the exponent of G′ divides that of G.

The idempotents e_ω and their relations are those of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition and its relation lemmas, which are stated for O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field of characteristic p and a finite abelian group H with p ∤ #H; both hold here for H = G′.
proofSteps: In O[G′] the idempotents e_χ are orthogonal (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition-api-1) with sum 1 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition-api-2). The O-algebra homomorphism O[G′] → O[G] induced by the inclusion (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom) carries both relations to O[G], so (e_χ)_χ is a complete family of orthogonal idempotents of O[G].
CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.bijective_pi: O[G] → ∏_χ O[G]/(1 − e_χ) is bijective.

By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/component-character-group-ring, (1 − e_χ)O[G] = ker α_{Ψ_χ}, so O[G]/(1 − e_χ) ≅ R_{Ψ_χ} compatibly with the projections from O[G] (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.quotientKerEquiv); composing gives the stated isomorphism.

Every ψ ∈ Ĝ restricts to exactly one χ ∈ Ĝ′, so the sets Ψ_χ are pairwise disjoint with union Ĝ. Each Ψ_χ is nonempty, because g′g_p ↦ χ(g′) is a character of G = G_p × G′ that restricts to χ. So the sets Ψ_χ partition Ĝ.
acceptance: G = G_p: one factor, O[G_p] ≅ R_Ĝ.
G = C_2 × C_p with p odd and C_2 = {1, h}: O[G] ≅ O[C_p] × O[C_p], the two factors being cut out by (1 + h)/2 and (1 − h)/2.

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source states the decomposition of O[G] into the components R_χ without proof. That the components are local is a separate theorem of this layer.

nodes.title: Norm quotients of a component
nodes.statement: (Dasgupta–Kakde Corollary 2.3.) For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and a subgroup I ⊆ G (the source takes I ⊆ G_p), R_χ/N_I R_χ ≅ R_Ψ with Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ, ψ(I) ≠ 1}; precisely, ker α_Ψ is generated by 1 − e_χ and N_I. In particular R_χ/N_I is a finite-index subring of a finite product of copies of O.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
The kernel description holds for any subgroup I; the source states I ⊆ G_p.
proofSteps: For ψ ∈ Ĝ ∖ Ψ_χ, ψ(e_χx) = 0, and for ψ ∈ Ψ_χ, ψ(e_χx) = ψ(x), because ψ(e_χ) is 1 on Ψ_χ and 0 off it (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-idempotent-evaluation). Hence α_Ψ(x) = 0 iff e_χx ∈ ker α_{{ψ : ψ(I) ≠ 1}}.
By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/norm-element-kernel that kernel is N_I·O[G]; so x = (1 − e_χ)x + e_χx lies in the ideal (1 − e_χ, N_I), and both generators lie in ker α_Ψ.
Reduce through R_χ ≅ O[G]/(1 − e_χ) (component-character-group-ring): R_χ/N_I R_χ ≅ O[G]/(1 − e_χ, N_I) ≅ R_Ψ.
The last assertion is PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-finite-index applied to this Ψ.
acceptance: I = 1 gives Ψ = ∅ and R_χ/R_χ = 0.
I = G′, which is not inside G_p unless G′ = 1: N_{G′} = #G′·e_1, so for χ = 1 the ideal (1 − e_1, N_{G′}) is O[G] and Ψ = ∅, and for χ ≠ 1 the ideal is (1 − e_χ) and Ψ = Ψ_χ.

sources.locator: Corollary 2.3, arXiv v3 PDF p. 16
sources.match: Corollary 2.3, which the source states without proof and for I ⊆ G_p; the steps above deduce it from Lemma 2.2 and the component description, for an arbitrary subgroup I.

nodes.title: Units of character group rings
nodes.statement: For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ and x ∈ R_Ψ: x is a unit of R_Ψ iff ψ(x) ∈ O^× for every ψ ∈ Ψ, and this holds iff ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} ψ(x) ∈ O^×. No locality of R_Ψ is assumed.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
Only that O is a commutative ring and that Ψ is finite is used.
proofSteps: The inclusion R_Ψ ⊆ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O is an injective integral ring homomorphism: ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O is a finite O-module (Ψ is finite), so each of its elements is integral over O (IsIntegral.of_finite), hence over the O-subalgebra R_Ψ (IsIntegral.tower_top for the tower O → R_Ψ → ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O). An injective integral ring homomorphism is local (RingHom.IsIntegral.isLocalHom: the inverse y of x in the product satisfies a monic equation y^n + a_1y^{n−1} + … + a_n = 0 over R_Ψ, and multiplying by x^{n−1} gives y = −(a_1 + a_2x + … + a_nx^{n−1}) ∈ R_Ψ). So if every ψ(x) is a unit of O, then x is a unit of the product (Pi.isUnit_iff) and therefore of R_Ψ.
Conversely the coordinate maps R_Ψ → O are ring homomorphisms, so they send units to units.
A finite product of elements of the commutative ring O is a unit iff every factor is (IsUnit.prod_iff).
acceptance: G = C_p, x = g ∈ R_Ĝ = O[C_p]: every ψ(g) is a root of unity, so g is a unit (with inverse g^{p−1}).
x = g − 1 in O[C_p]: ψ(x) = 0 for ψ = 1, so x is not a unit.
R_Ψ need not be local: for p ∤ #G, G ≠ 1 and Ψ = Ĝ, R_Ĝ = ∏_{ψ} O is a product of #G ≥ 2 copies of O, and the criterion is the description of the units of a product.

sources.locator: §2.3, arXiv v3 PDF p. 18
sources.match: The source uses the criterion for the character group ring O[G]^− (all odd characters), which is not local as soon as G′ has more than one odd character, and gives no proof; the first step above proves it for every Ψ.

sources.locator: §5.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34
sources.match: For the local ring R = O[G_p]_χ the source passes from ∏ψ(x) ∈ O^× to every ψ(x) ∈ O^× and then to x ∈ R^×, giving as reason that the maps R → O are local homomorphisms of local rings.

nodes.title: Units of a character group ring of one component are detected by one character
nodes.statement: Let χ ∈ Ĝ′ and let Ψ be a nonempty subset of Ψ_χ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ}. For x ∈ R_Ψ the following are equivalent: x is a unit of R_Ψ; ψ(x) ∈ O^× for some ψ ∈ Ψ; ψ(x) ∈ O^× for every ψ ∈ Ψ. The reason is the congruence ψ(x) ≡ ψ′(x) mod 𝔪_O for x ∈ O[G] and ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ_χ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
Ψ is nonempty: for Ψ = ∅ the ring R_∅ is zero, every element of it is a unit, and there is no character.
What is used: O is a local ring whose residue field has characteristic p, and for ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ the character ψ′ψ^{-1} has p-power order (it is trivial on G′, so it factors through the p-group G_p).
proofSteps: For ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ_χ the character ψ′ψ^{-1} is trivial on G′, so its values are p-power roots of unity of O. A p-power root of unity ζ of O is ≡ 1 mod 𝔪_O: its image ζ̄ in the residue field k, of characteristic p, satisfies ζ̄^{p^n} = 1, hence ζ̄ = 1 (ExpChar.pow_prime_pow_mul_eq_one_iff with m = 1).
Hence for x = Σ_g a_g g ∈ O[G], ψ′(x) − ψ(x) = Σ_g a_g ψ(g)((ψ′ψ^{-1})(g) − 1) ∈ 𝔪_O. In the local ring O an element congruent modulo 𝔪_O to a unit is a unit, so ψ(x) ∈ O^× iff ψ′(x) ∈ O^×.
By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-criterion, x is a unit of R_Ψ iff every ψ(x), ψ ∈ Ψ, is a unit; by the previous step and Ψ ≠ ∅ this holds iff one of them is.
acceptance: G = C_p, Ψ = Ĝ, x = Σ_i a_i g^i ∈ O[C_p]: x is a unit iff the augmentation Σ_i a_i is a unit of O.

Across two components one unit value does not suffice: for G = G′ = C_2 = {1, h} and p odd, the element (1 + h)/2 has value 1 at the trivial character and 0 at the sign character, and it is not a unit.

sources.locator: §5.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34
sources.match: The source uses, for R = O[G_p]_χ and one character ψ belonging to χ, that ψ(x) ∈ O^× implies x ∈ R^×; its only justification is the remark of §5.1 that the maps R → O are local homomorphisms of local rings.

nodes.title: Character group rings of one component are local
nodes.statement: For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ (for instance R_χ itself, or R_χ/N_I for a nontrivial subgroup I ⊆ G_p), R_Ψ is a local ring, and its maximal ideal is 𝔪_Ψ = {x ∈ R_Ψ : ψ(x) ∈ 𝔪_O}, for any ψ ∈ Ψ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).

The two instances are nonempty. The character g′g_p ↦ χ(g′) of G = G_p × G′ lies in Ψ_χ. For a nontrivial subgroup I ⊆ G_p some character ψ_p of G_p is nontrivial on I (CommGroup.exists_apply_ne_one_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity for G_p, whose exponent divides that of G), and g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)ψ_p(g_p) lies in Ψ_χ and is nontrivial on I.
proofSteps: By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-one-character, for every ψ ∈ Ψ an element x ∈ R_Ψ is a unit iff ψ(x) ∈ O^×. So the set of non-units of R_Ψ is 𝔪_Ψ = ev_ψ^{-1}(𝔪_O): it does not depend on ψ, and it is the kernel of the ring homomorphism R_Ψ → O → k, hence an ideal.
R_Ψ ≠ 0 because Ψ ≠ ∅ and O ≠ 0. A nonzero ring whose non-units are closed under addition is local (IsLocalRing.of_nonunits_add), and its maximal ideal is the set of non-units, here 𝔪_Ψ.
acceptance: Ψ = Ψ_1 for G = G_p: R_Ψ = O[G_p] is local, and its maximal ideal is the preimage of 𝔪_O under the augmentation.
Ψ spanning two components (χ ≠ χ′) gives R_Ψ ≅ R_{Ψ∩Ψ_χ} × R_{Ψ∩Ψ_χ′}, which is not local.
Ψ = ∅ is excluded: R_∅ = 0 is not a local ring.

sources.locator: §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15
sources.match: The source asserts without proof that each component R_χ = O[G_p]_χ is local; this is the case Ψ = Ψ_χ of the theorem.

sources.locator: §5.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34
sources.match: The source treats R = O[G_p]_χ as a local ring here; that each character induces a local homomorphism R → O is the separate lemma on the evaluations.

sources.locator: §7.2.9, arXiv v3 PDF p. 49
sources.match: Stated without proof. In §7.2.9 the letter Ψ is not an arbitrary set of characters: from the end of §7.1 on, R denotes R_Ψ for the trivial-zero-free set Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ, ψ(v) ≠ 1 for all v ∈ Σ}, a subset of the characters belonging to one χ. The theorem proves locality for every nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ. Nonemptiness is needed (R_∅ = 0 is not local) and is left implicit in the source; for a Ψ meeting two components R_Ψ is not local.

sources.locator: §7.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 43
sources.match: Fixes what R = R_Ψ means in §7.2.9: the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient of the component O[G_p]_χ.

nodes.title: A power of the maximal ideal of a character group ring lies in 𝔪_O R_Ψ
nodes.statement: For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ, let 𝔪_Ψ be the maximal ideal of the local ring R_Ψ. Then 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ, and there is N ≥ 1 with 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ. Hence the powers of 𝔪_Ψ and of 𝔪_O R_Ψ define the same topology on R_Ψ.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
What is used: O is a local ring, R_Ψ is a local ring and a finite O-module, and 𝔪_Ψ = ev_ψ^{-1}(𝔪_O) for the O-linear evaluation ev_ψ. Completeness of O is not used.

The hypothesis on Ψ enters only through the locality of R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local); the statement holds for every Ψ for which R_Ψ is a local ring and a finite O-module.
proofSteps: 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ: for a ∈ 𝔪_O and y ∈ R_Ψ, ev_ψ(a·y) = a·ev_ψ(y) ∈ 𝔪_O, and 𝔪_Ψ = ev_ψ^{-1}(𝔪_O) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local).

A = R_Ψ/𝔪_O R_Ψ is a finite module over the field k = O/𝔪_O, because R_Ψ is a finite O-module (it is a quotient of O[G]); hence A is an artinian ring (IsArtinianRing.of_finite). It is a local ring, as a quotient of the local ring R_Ψ by a proper ideal, with maximal ideal 𝔪_Ψ/𝔪_O R_Ψ, and this is its Jacobson radical (IsLocalRing.jacobson_eq_maximalIdeal for the zero ideal).

The Jacobson radical of an artinian ring is nilpotent (IsArtinianRing.isNilpotent_jacobson_bot): (𝔪_Ψ/𝔪_O R_Ψ)^N = 0 for some N, which can be taken ≥ 1. That is, 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ. Consequently (𝔪_O R_Ψ)^n ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ^n and 𝔪_Ψ^{Nn} ⊆ (𝔪_O R_Ψ)^n for every n.
acceptance: G = G_p = C_p, Ψ = Ĝ: 𝔪_Ψ = (π, g − 1) with π a uniformiser of O, and (g − 1)^p ≡ g^p − 1 = 0 modulo p, so N = p works.
The exponent depends on G: for O = Z_p and G = C_{p^n}, O[G]/pO[G] = F_p[x]/(x − 1)^{p^n}, and the least N is p^n.
p ∤ #G: Ψ = {χ}, R_Ψ = O, 𝔪_Ψ = 𝔪_O and N = 1.

sources.locator: §7.2.9, arXiv v3 PDF p. 49
sources.match: The source asserts completeness without proof. This lemma is the comparison of the 𝔪_Ψ-adic and 𝔪_O-adic filtrations on which the proof of completeness rests; the source does not state it.

nodes.title: The evaluations of a character group ring of one component are local homomorphisms
nodes.statement: For χ ∈ Ĝ′, a subset Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ} and ψ ∈ Ψ, the evaluation ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O is a local homomorphism: if ev_ψ(x) is a unit of O, then x is a unit of R_Ψ. Since R_Ψ and O are local rings, this says ev_ψ(𝔪_Ψ) ⊆ 𝔪_O.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
Ψ is nonempty because it contains ψ. A local homomorphism is one that reflects units (Mathlib's IsLocalHom); the locality of R_Ψ is not used in the proof.
proofSteps: Let x ∈ R_Ψ with ev_ψ(x) ∈ O^×. By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-one-character, applied to the nonempty set Ψ and its element ψ, x is a unit of R_Ψ. This is the defining property of IsLocalHom for the homomorphism ev_ψ (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.eval).
acceptance: G = G_p = C_p, Ψ = Ĝ, ψ = 1: an element of O[C_p] whose augmentation is a unit of O is a unit.

The restriction to one component is needed: for G = G′ = C_2 = {1, h}, p odd and Ψ = Ĝ, the evaluation at the trivial character sends (1 + h)/2 to 1, and (1 + h)/2 is not a unit of R_Ĝ = O[G] (its value at the sign character is 0).

sources.locator: §5.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34
sources.match: The source asserts this for R = O[G_p]_χ and gives no proof; the lemma proves it for every character group ring R_Ψ with Ψ inside the characters belonging to one χ.

nodes.title: The residue field of a character group ring of one component
nodes.statement: For χ ∈ Ĝ′, a subset Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ and ψ ∈ Ψ, the homomorphism of residue fields R_Ψ/𝔪_Ψ → O/𝔪_O = k induced by the local homomorphism ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O is bijective. So the residue field of the local ring R_Ψ is k.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).

R_Ψ is a local ring by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local, and ev_ψ is a local homomorphism by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-eval-local-hom; the induced map of residue fields is IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map.

The hypothesis on Ψ enters only through the locality of R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local) and through PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-eval-local-hom; the statement holds for every Ψ for which R_Ψ is a local ring, a finite O-module, and ev_ψ is a local homomorphism.
proofSteps: The induced map R_Ψ/𝔪_Ψ → k is a homomorphism of fields, hence injective.

It is surjective: it sends the class of x to the class of ev_ψ(x) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map_residue), ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O is surjective (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.eval_surjective), and O → k is surjective.
acceptance: G = G_p, Ψ = Ĝ, ψ = 1: the residue map of O[G_p] is Σ_g a_g g ↦ Σ_g ā_g ∈ k.
p ∤ #G: Ψ = {χ}, R_Ψ ≅ O through ev_χ and the map is the identity of k.
For ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ the two induced maps agree, because ψ(x) ≡ ψ′(x) mod 𝔪_O.

The source's description of the maximal ideal: 𝔪_Ψ is generated by a uniformiser π of O and the elements α_Ψ(g) − χ(g′), g = g′g_p ∈ G. These elements lie in 𝔪_Ψ (ev_ψ sends α_Ψ(g) − χ(g′) to χ(g′)(ψ(g_p) − 1) ∈ 𝔪_O), and the quotient of R_Ψ by them is a quotient of k[G]/(g − χ̄(g′) : g ∈ G) = k that maps onto k.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.22, arXiv v3 PDF p. 64
sources.match: The source states, for the trivial-zero-free ring R = R_Ψ of §7.1 and without proof, that 𝔪_R is generated by a uniformiser of O and the elements [g] − χ(g), and that R/𝔪_R ≅ k_E; the lemma proves the second assertion for every Ψ inside the characters belonging to one χ.

nodes.title: Character group rings of one component are complete noetherian local rings
nodes.statement: For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ, the local ring R_Ψ is noetherian, and it is complete and separated for the 𝔪_Ψ-adic topology, which coincides with its 𝔪_O-adic topology because 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ for some N ≥ 1 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-maximal-ideal-power). So R_Ψ is a complete noetherian local O-algebra.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
What is used beyond locality: O is a noetherian local ring that is 𝔪_O-adically complete and separated, and R_Ψ is a finite O-module.

The hypothesis on Ψ enters only through the locality of R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local); the statement holds for every Ψ for which R_Ψ is a local ring and a finite O-module.
proofSteps: R_Ψ is a finite O-module (a finite free one by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-lattice) and O is noetherian, so R_Ψ is a noetherian ring (IsNoetherianRing.of_finite).

By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-maximal-ideal-power, 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ for some N ≥ 1; here 𝔪_Ψ is the maximal ideal of the local ring R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local).

R_Ψ is 𝔪_O-adically complete and separated as an O-module. Separated: R_Ψ is a finite module over the noetherian local ring O (IsHausdorff.of_isLocalRing, the Krull intersection theorem). Precomplete: by AdicCompletion.of_surjective_iff it suffices that the canonical map of : R_Ψ → AdicCompletion 𝔪_O R_Ψ is surjective. The map AdicCompletion 𝔪_O O ⊗_O R_Ψ → AdicCompletion 𝔪_O R_Ψ, r ⊗ x ↦ r·of(x) (AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct), is surjective because R_Ψ is a finite O-module (AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct_surjective_of_finite), and every r ∈ AdicCompletion 𝔪_O O is of(a) with a ∈ O because O is complete (AdicCompletion.of_surjective_iff for O); since of(a)·of(x) = of(a·x), every element of AdicCompletion 𝔪_O R_Ψ is of(y) with y ∈ R_Ψ.
From the O-module to the ring: by IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff, R_Ψ is complete and separated as a module over itself for the ideal J = 𝔪_O R_Ψ.

From J to 𝔪_Ψ: J^n ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ^n and 𝔪_Ψ^{Nn} ⊆ J^n for all n, so the J-adic topology of R_Ψ is also 𝔪_Ψ-adic (isAdic_iff: the powers of 𝔪_Ψ are open and every neighbourhood of 0 contains one of them). Completeness and separatedness of an adic ring depend only on its topology (IsAdic.isAdicComplete_iff, applied to J and to 𝔪_Ψ), so R_Ψ is 𝔪_Ψ-adically complete and separated.
acceptance: Ψ = Ψ_1 for G = G_p = C_p: O[C_p] is a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal (π, g − 1), π a uniformiser of O, and (g − 1)^p ∈ p·O[C_p] because (g − 1)^p ≡ g^p − 1 = 0 modulo p.
R = R_Ψ for the trivial-zero-free set Ψ of Dasgupta–Kakde §7.1, when that set is nonempty, is a complete local Z_p-algebra, as §7.2.9 asserts.

sources.locator: §7.2.9, arXiv v3 PDF p. 49
sources.match: Stated without proof, for the trivial-zero-free set Ψ of §7.1, a subset of the characters belonging to one χ; the theorem proves completeness for every nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ.

sources.locator: §7.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 43

nodes.title: The order of a principal quotient of a character group ring
nodes.statement: (Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 2.5.) For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ and a non-zerodivisor x ∈ R_Ψ, the quotient R_Ψ/xR_Ψ is finite and #(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O/(∏_{ψ∈Ψ} ψ(x))).
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).

What is used: O is a Dedekind domain (a discrete valuation ring) that is infinite (characteristic zero), #G ≠ 0 in O, and O/(a) is finite for every a ≠ 0; G is finite. The last condition is Ring.HasFiniteQuotients O. That class has no instance for a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field in the pinned Mathlib (only for finite rings, ℤ and rings of integers of number fields), so in the Dasgupta–Kakde setting it is derived as in the second proof step.
proofSteps: R_Ψ ⊆ O_Ψ := ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O has finite index (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-finite-index), and x is a non-zerodivisor of O_Ψ with every ψ(x) ≠ 0 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-nonzerodivisor).

O_Ψ/xO_Ψ = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O/(ψ(x)) is finite, because every ψ(x) is nonzero and O/(a) is finite for a ≠ 0 (a nonzero ideal of the discrete valuation ring O is (ϖ^n) = 𝔪_O^n for a uniformiser ϖ, by IsDiscreteValuationRing.ideal_eq_span_pow_irreducible, and O/𝔪_O^n is finite by Ideal.finite_quotient_pow, because 𝔪_O is principal and the residue field O/𝔪_O is finite; this is Ring.HasFiniteQuotients O). Multiplication by x is an isomorphism O_Ψ/R_Ψ ≅ xO_Ψ/xR_Ψ, so [xO_Ψ : xR_Ψ] = [O_Ψ : R_Ψ] is finite. Multiplicativity of the index in the towers xR_Ψ ⊆ R_Ψ ⊆ O_Ψ and xR_Ψ ⊆ xO_Ψ ⊆ O_Ψ (Submodule.card_quotient_mul_card_quotient) gives [O_Ψ : R_Ψ]·#(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ)·[xO_Ψ : xR_Ψ], and cancelling the equal finite nonzero factors gives #(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ).

#(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ) = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} #(O/ψ(x)) = #(O/∏ψ(x)); the last equality is cardQuot_mul applied to the principal ideals (ψ(x)) of O, which is a Dedekind domain (a discrete valuation ring) and infinite (characteristic zero).

sources.locator: Lemma 2.5, arXiv v3 PDF p. 17
sources.match: Lemma 2.5 and its proof. The proof uses that x is a non-zerodivisor of O_Ψ, while the hypothesis gives it in R_Ψ: the same unproved transfer as in the proof of Lemma 2.4 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E18); here every factor is the infinite ring O, the transfer holds, and the lemma on non-zerodivisors supplies it. Finiteness of R_Ψ/xR_Ψ, implicit in the source, is part of the statement.

nodes.title: The involution # and the rings R^#
nodes.statement: The involution # of O[G] is the O-algebra automorphism g ↦ g^{-1} (the antipode of the commutative Hopf algebra O[G]); (x^#)^# = x and ψ(x^#) = ψ^{-1}(x) for every character ψ. For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ put Ψ^# = Ψ^{-1} = {ψ^{-1} : ψ ∈ Ψ} and R^# = R_{Ψ^#} for R = R_Ψ. Then # maps ker α_Ψ onto ker α_{Ψ^#} and induces mutually inverse O-algebra isomorphisms # : R_Ψ → R_{Ψ^#} and # : R_{Ψ^#} → R_Ψ, with #(α_Ψ(x)) = α_{Ψ^#}(x^#) and (#y)(ψ^{-1}) = y(ψ). It is an endomorphism of R_Ψ only when Ψ^# = Ψ. For R = O[G] (and Z_p[G], Z[G]) R^# = R. Ideals transport as I^# = #(I) ⊆ R^#; in particular (xR)^# = x^#R^#.
hypotheses: Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
The construction of # on O[G] needs only O commutative and G commutative.
proofSteps: # is HopfAlgebra.antipodeAlgHom O O[G], for the Hopf algebra structure MonoidAlgebra.instHopfAlgebra of O[G] over O (the coefficient Hopf algebra is O itself); it is an algebra map because O[G] is commutative, G being commutative. MonoidAlgebra.antipode_single gives antipode(a·g) = antipode_O(a)·g^{-1}, and the antipode of O is the identity (CommSemiring.antipode_eq_id), so # sends a·g to a·g^{-1}; hence it agrees with MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom of invMonoidHom. Involutivity (x^#)^# = x is TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.antipode_antipode, and # as a self-inverse automorphism is TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.antipodeAlgEquiv for A = O[G].
ψ(g^#) = ψ(g^{-1}) = ψ(g)^{-1} = ψ^{-1}(g) on group elements (character-evaluation, TauCeti.charEval_of), hence on O[G] by linearity.

Therefore x ∈ ker α_Ψ iff x^# ∈ ker α_{Ψ^#} (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.ker_proj). So α_{Ψ^#} ∘ # is surjective with kernel ker α_Ψ and factors through an isomorphism R_Ψ → R_{Ψ^#} (TauCeti.charGroupRing.lift); the same construction for Ψ^# gives its inverse, because # ∘ # = id and (Ψ^#)^# = Ψ.

In the Dasgupta–Kakde setting ker α_Ψ determines Ψ: for ψ′ ∈ Ĝ ∖ Ψ the element e = Σ_g ψ′(g)^{-1} g has ψ(e) = 0 for every character ψ ≠ ψ′ and ψ′(e) = #G ≠ 0 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-scaled-idempotent for the set Ĝ and its element ψ′); so e lies in ker α_Ψ, and Ψ is the set of characters vanishing on ker α_Ψ. If # maps ker α_Ψ into itself, then ker α_{Ψ^#} = #(ker α_Ψ) ⊆ ker α_Ψ by the previous step, so Ψ ⊆ Ψ^#, and applying ψ ↦ ψ^{-1} gives Ψ^# ⊆ Ψ. Hence # maps ker α_Ψ into itself only when Ψ^# = Ψ.
acceptance: G′ = ⟨τ⟩ ≅ C_3 (p ≠ 3), χ(τ) = ζ_3: # maps the component R_χ onto the different component R_{χ^{-1}}.
For Ψ = Ĝ, # is the automorphism # of O[G] ≅ R_Ĝ.

nodes.title: The contragredient dual
nodes.statement: For a ring isomorphism σ : S → R of commutative rings (σ = # : R^# → R for R = R_Ψ, or # : R → R for R = O[G], Z_p[G], Z[G]) and an R-module M, the contragredient dual M^* = Hom_R(M, R) is the S-module with (s·φ)(x) = φ(σ(s)·x); for R = R_Ψ this is Dasgupta–Kakde's rule (r·φ)(x) = φ(r^#·x). A linear map f : M → N induces the S-linear f^* : N^* → M^*, φ ↦ φ∘f, functorially; for M = R^m, M^* is free over S on the dual basis.
hypotheses: R and S are commutative rings and σ is a ring isomorphism; the module structure is Module.compHom along σ.

The source states the rule for Z[G]-modules, with M^* = Hom_{Z[G]}(M, Z[G]), and applies it to modules over a character group ring R = R_Ψ. For an R-module the dual is Hom_R(M, R), the reading that Lemma 6.1 requires. The general form, with a ring isomorphism σ : S → R, covers both.
proofSteps: Give Module.Dual R M the S-module structure Module.compHom along σ; (s·φ)(x) = σ(s)φ(x) = φ(σ(s)x) by R-linearity of φ.
f^* is LinearMap.dualMap f, φ ↦ φ∘f, which is S-linear for the transported structures; the identity and composition laws hold for dualMap.

For M = R^m the dual basis identifies M^* with R^m (Module.piEquiv with values in R), and σ^{-1} coordinatewise identifies it with S^m: φ ↦ (σ^{-1}(φ(e_i)))_i, which is S-linear because σ^{-1}(σ(s)·φ(e_i)) = s·σ^{-1}(φ(e_i)). For an m×n matrix A, (φ∘A)(e_j) = Σ_i A_{ij}·φ(e_i), so the dual of A becomes the n×m matrix with (j, i) entry σ^{-1}(A_{ij}).

Semilinear form: for φ ∈ M^* the map σ^{-1}∘φ : M → S is additive and σ^{-1}-semilinear, an element of Mathlib's S-module of semilinear maps (LinearMap along the ring homomorphism σ^{-1}); φ ↦ σ^{-1}∘φ is bijective with inverse ψ ↦ σ∘ψ, and σ^{-1}((s·φ)(x)) = s·σ^{-1}(φ(x)), so it is S-linear for the pointwise structure.

Group rings: for a finite commutative group G, R = S = O[G] and σ = #, the map Ψ : Hom_O(M, O) → M^*, Ψ_f(m) = Σ_{g∈G} f(g·m)·g^{-1}, takes values in O[G]-linear maps (Ψ_f(h·m) = h·Ψ_f(m)), has inverse φ ↦ (the coefficient of 1 in φ(·)), and satisfies Ψ_{f∘h^{-1}} = h·Ψ_f for h ∈ G; so the action of G on M^* corresponds to Mathlib's dual representation Representation.dual.

Products and projectivity: Module.dualProdDualEquivDual, (φ, ψ) ↦ φ∘fst + ψ∘snd, is S-linear for the contragredient structures, since s acts on all three duals as σ(s). If M is a finitely generated projective R-module, Module.Dual R M is finitely generated and projective over R (Module.dual_finite, Module.dual_projective). The bijection toDual : M^* → Module.Dual R M is σ-semilinear, so M^* is projective over S (Module.Projective.of_equiv, with σ and σ^{-1} as the two mutually inverse ring homomorphisms), and a finite generating set of Module.Dual R M over R generates M^* over S because σ is surjective.
acceptance: σ = id: M^* is the ordinary dual Hom_R(M, R).
For R = S = O[G] and σ = #: the inverse of the isomorphism Hom_O(M, O) → M^* of equivDualOfGroupRing sends φ to the functional m ↦ (the coefficient of 1 in φ(m)).

nodes.title: Quadratically presented modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring. A quadratic presentation of an R-module N consists of an integer m ≥ 1, an m×m matrix φ over R and a surjection π : R^m → N whose kernel is the image of φ : R^m → R^m; N is quadratically presented over R if it has one, equivalently N ≅ coker(φ) for a square matrix φ of size m ≥ 1.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
m ≥ 1 is part of the definition (the zero module is presented by R →(1) R).
proofSteps: Record (m, φ, π) with π surjective and range(φ) = ker(π). The Mathlib presentation with generators and relations indexed by Fin m (the j-th relation is the j-th column of φ, the i-th variable is π(e_i)) is a presentation by Module.Relations.Solution.isPresentation_iff, so a quadratically presented module is finitely presented (Module.Presentation.finitePresentation).

Base change: R′ ⊗_R − applied to the exact sequence R^m → R^m → N → 0 gives an exact sequence whose last map is surjective (lTensor_exact, the right exactness of the tensor product); under R′ ⊗_R R^m ≅ R′^m its first map is the image matrix.

Direct sums use the block-diagonal matrix, of size m + m′ and determinant det φ·det φ′ (Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁ with zero upper-right block); transport along an isomorphism composes π and keeps the matrix (Module.Presentation.ofLinearEquiv on the Mathlib side); coker(φ) is presented by φ and the quotient map (compare Module.Presentation.cokernel). Mathlib has no base change of a Module.Presentation along a ring map at the pin, so base change is built here.

The isomorphism R^m/φR^m ≅ N: π induces R^m/ker π ≅ N (LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective), and ker π = range φ. Together with cokernel and ofLinearEquiv this is the equivalence with N ≅ coker(φ) in the statement.
acceptance: R/(a) is presented by R →(a) R; R^m by the zero m×m matrix.
Over Z_p⟦T⟧, F_p = Z_p⟦T⟧/(p, T) is not quadratically presented.
ofPresentation applied to toPresentation of a quadratic presentation (m, φ, π), with the identity bijections, returns (m, φ, π).

tests.name: not_quadratic_residue_field
tests.statement: Over R = Z_p⟦T⟧ the module R/(p, T) is not quadratically presented. R is a noetherian domain and its maximal ideal (p, T) has height 2 (0 ⊂ (T) ⊂ (p, T)), so the module vanishes after localising at (0) and at every height-one prime. If it were coker(φ) for a square matrix φ, then φ would be surjective, hence invertible, after each of these localisations, so det φ would be a nonzero element lying in no height-one prime, hence a unit (a minimal prime over a nonzero non-unit of a noetherian domain has height one: Krull's principal ideal theorem), and coker(φ) would be 0.

nodes.title: The Fitting ideal of a quadratic presentation
nodes.statement: If N has a quadratic presentation R^m →φ R^m → N → 0, then Fitt_R(N) = (det φ); in particular Fitt_R(N) is principal.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.

Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the initial Fitting ideal of a finitely presented R-module M: the ideal generated by the n×n minors of the relation matrix of any finite presentation with n generators, independent of the presentation and compatible with base change. It is the finite-presentation Fitting-ideal carrier imported from the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 1 (accepted RS-16).
proofSteps: N is finitely presented (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation), and (π, φ) is a finite presentation with m generators. By presentation independence of the imported Fitting ideal, Fitt_R(N) is generated by the m×m minors of φ.
The only m×m minor of the m×m matrix φ is det φ.
acceptance: N = R/(a): Fitt = (a).
N = R^m: Fitt = (det 0) = 0 for m ≥ 1.

R = Z_p⟦T⟧, N = R/(p, T): Fitt_R(N) = (p, T) is not principal, so N is not quadratically presented (the test not_quadratic_residue_field of quadratic-presentation, which is proved there without Fitting ideals).
