sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 13.1, printed p. 189 / PDF 90, and Definition 13.3, printed p. 190 / PDF 91; the same text in arXiv v2 PDF 65.
sourceIssues.printed: The general coefficient-DVR structure theorem and characteristic-ideal display use powers of the rational prime for vertical elementary factors.
sourceIssues.correction: Over Λ = O_L⟦T⟧ the μ-part is ⊕ Λ/(ϖ^{n_i}) for a uniformizer ϖ of O_L, and Ch_Λ(M) = (ϖ^n)∏(f_j^{m_j}). The printed forms are right when L/ℚ_p is unramified (then p is a uniformizer).
sourceIssues.reason: Take L = ℚ_p(√p), ϖ = √p, M = Λ/(ϖ). The prime (ϖ) has height one, and the length of M at (ϖ) is 1. Pseudo-isomorphism (finite kernel and cokernel) preserves lengths at height-one primes. Λ/(p^n) = Λ/(ϖ^{2n}) has length 2n at (ϖ), Λ/(f^m) with f distinguished has length 0 there, and Λ^r is not torsion. So M is not pseudo-isomorphic to any module of the printed form, and (p^n) cannot equal (ϖ) = Ch_Λ(M). The cited Washington Theorem 13.12 is over ℤ_p⟦T⟧. RJW's distinguished polynomials use the maximal ideal 𝔭 (fraktur), while the μ-part uses the roman p, as the rendered pages show.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 3.9 (TeX label l:coker), last display of the proof and the sentence after it, arXiv:2010.00657v3 PDF p. 26; the same text is on PDF p. 26 of the authors' copy dated 15 February 2022.
sourceIssues.printed: The higher-adjugate argument places the adjugate on the left of the compound matrix and uses the resulting equality to conclude that the determinant multiple is in the image of the compound map.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the right-sided identity C_r(A′)·adj_r(A′) = det(A′)·I and the vector adj_r(A′)x extended by zero to ι_J(adj_r(A′)x) ∈ ⋀^r R^n: det(A′)x = C_r(A′)(adj_r(A′)x) = C_r(A)(ι_J(adj_r(A′)x)), which lies in the image of C_r(A).
sourceIssues.reason: The display writes det(A′)x as adj_r(A′) applied to C_r(A)x̃, an element of the image of C_r(A) (the matrices act on column vectors: x̃ ∈ ⋀^r R^n, x ∈ ⋀^r R^m). To conclude that det(A′)x itself lies in the image one needs either the identity with the factors in the other order, C_r(A′)·adj_r(A′) = det(A′)·I, applied to the vector adj_r(A′)x extended by zero (the correction), or that the image of C_r(A) is stable under adj_r(A′). The proof states neither. The image is in fact stable, but that needs an argument of its own for 1 < r < m, so the printed step is unproved rather than false. Lemma 3.9 itself is true.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.4 (TeX label l:size), proof, displays (27) and (28) and the sentences after them, arXiv:2010.00657v3 PDF p. 17 (statement on PDF p. 16). The authors' copy dated 15 February 2022, an earlier text, has the same statement, the same two displays and the same quoted sentence on its PDF pp. 16–17 ((27) on p. 16, the sentence on p. 17); its proof does not write out the step for PIDs, and its sentence after (28) ends ‘in the denominator’.
sourceIssues.printed: The proof claims that multiplying by the non-zerodivisor det(A) identifies the numerator space isomorphically with the denominator space.
sourceIssues.correction: det(A) is by hypothesis a non-zerodivisor of B, not of the product B′ = ∏ D_i, and the step needs it on B′. It is one whenever no factor D_i is a finite field (so for products of DVRs, and in every use in the paper): B ∩ D_i has finite index in the infinite ring D_i, hence is nonzero, and a vanishing component x_i = 0 would give x·(B ∩ D_i) = 0. With a finite-field factor the step can fail, but the lemma is still true: let K = B ∩ ∏_{D_i finite} D_i, a finite ideal of B. Multiplication by x is injective, hence bijective, on K, so A is bijective on K^m (adjugate), and therefore B^m/AB^m ≅ (B/K)^m/A(B/K)^m and B/xB ≅ (B/K)/x(B/K). The ring B/K is a finite-index subring of the product of the infinite factors, the image of x is a non-zerodivisor of it (if xy ∈ K then xy = xk with k ∈ K, so y = k), and the printed argument applies to B/K.
sourceIssues.reason: Take B = {(a, a mod p) : a ∈ Z} inside B′ = Z × F_p, and x = (p, 0). The subring has index p and is isomorphic to Z. For the 1×1 presentation A = (x), x is a non-zerodivisor of B and B/xB has p elements, although x annihilates (0,1) in B′. Here B′/xB′ has p² elements, B′/B has p elements, and xB′ = xB = pZ × 0. Consequently the multiplier map B′/B → xB′/xB is zero and cannot be an isomorphism; the ratios in (27) and (28) are p. The subsequent cancellation of det(A) on the ambient module in the argument for (28) has the same missing hypothesis. Fields are PIDs, so the example satisfies Lemma 2.4 as stated. Its conclusion remains true, as does the general statement after the finite-ideal reduction in the correction. If fields are excluded from the intended PID convention, the ambient non-zerodivisor property is valid but still requires its own argument. The middle ratio in (27) also has an extra cardinality marker inside its denominator; that separate typographical slip has no mathematical effect.

sourceIssues.locator: §6.1, the paragraph after (81) (TeX line 1537), arXiv:2010.00657v3 PDF p. 40; the same sentence, with the rule numbered (83), is on PDF p. 41 of the authors' copy dated 15 February 2022.
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses rule (80) to equip M∗ with an R#-module structure whenever M is an R-module.
sourceIssues.correction: For a module M over a character group ring R = R_Ψ, M^* has to be read as Hom_R(M, R), with r ∈ R^# acting by (r·ϕ)(x) = ϕ(r^#·x), r^# ∈ R. The dual defined just before (80), M^* := Hom_{Z[G]}(M, Z[G]), is the intended object only when M is considered over the ring Z[G] itself; an R_Ψ-module is also a Z[G]-module, and for it that dual is 0.
sourceIssues.reason: R_Ψ is an algebra over O ⊇ Z_p, and Hom_Z(M, Z) = 0 for every Z_p-module M (Hom_Z(Z_p, Z) = 0, because Z_p is divisible by every prime ℓ ≠ p), so the dual as defined, Hom_{Z[G]}(M, Z[G]) ⊆ Hom_Z(M, Z[G]), is 0 for every R_Ψ-module M. Lemma 6.1 on the same page (the transpose of a quadratic presentation with matrix (a_ij) over R is presented over R^# by (a_ji^#)) needs (R^m)^* ≅ (R^#)^m, that is, the dual Hom_R(−, R). The intended meaning is clear and nothing downstream is affected.

reviewHistory.notes: Independent review of FIX-RT-AREA-iwasawa-2~2 (Claude Code, session claude-6ZAIEy, pull request #6786), which applied the confirmed red-team finding RT-AREA-iwasawa-2/4 here by adding 25 L6 nodes for the ring theory of Dasgupta–Kakde (arXiv:2010.00657v3); reviewer Claude, session claude-D9I0pm. Scope: those nodes, the baseline declarations they cite, the request to StableReduction Layer 1, source finding E17 and the L6 block of the suggested file. The 436 earlier nodes were not read again. Verdict needs_changes, for two reasons, neither of them a mathematical error left in the L6 plan. (1) The L6 section of the reader document (research/blueprint/readmes/PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras.md, not a deliverable of this review) still describes the 25 nodes as the fix wrote them; it has to be regenerated from the packet, which now has 50 L6 nodes. (2) The eight acceptance blockers of independent-review-REV-PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras (needs_changes, 2026-10-05) concern L4, were not touched by the fix and remain open; that review object, with its 436 per-node rows, is preserved verbatim as the last entry of reviewHistory. They belong to the revision BP-PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras~2, not to a further fix round. Checked: every node against the source (TeX and PDF text of arXiv v3 fetched again, SHA-256 as recorded; every excerpt found on the page its locator names); every example, test and number recomputed exactly; every cited library declaration read at the pinned commits; ownership against accepted RS-16 and every packet of the atlas. Two readings were made, the second by readers who were not shown the findings of the first: 215 findings (12 errors, 92 gaps, 111 minor), all applied here or answered in the report. Main corrections. (a) Declarations the fix planned afresh are in the pinned libraries and are now cited instead: the character evaluation (TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point), the augmentation, the antipode as an involutive algebra equivalence, the subgroup character sum for norm elements and idempotents, column orthogonality of characters, 2×2 minors with Cauchy–Binet, Mathlib's HasEnoughRootsOfUnity for the coefficient hypothesis and Module.Presentation for presentations. (b) Ownership of Fitting ideals follows RS-16: the request to StableReduction Layer 1 is narrowed to the initial Fitting ideal of finitely presented modules, the source's own convention, and the higher Fitting ideals are planned in L6. (c) Statements: Lemma 2.4 is restored to the source's generality with a complete proof; (171) is stated for projective presentations of constant rank, as the source uses it; the sign in the block matrix of Lemma 2.6, a false remark on Z_p[G]-algebras, a hypothesis that fails for power-series coefficients and tests that fail in degenerate cases are corrected. (d) Granularity: the roadmap is planned at lemma level, so bundled theorem nodes were split; 25 nodes were added. (e) Proofs: every library fact a step names is now a prerequisite; the baseline grew from 383 to 525 declarations. Source findings: E17 confirmed with a reworded reason; E18 (an error in the proof of Lemma 2.4, whose statement stands), E19 and E20 added and confirmed against arXiv v3 and the authors' copy; the Annals version could not be opened. Suggested Lean file: the L6 block was rewritten to follow the corrected packet (the 172 API items, 50 node declarations and 57 unit tests of L6, each under the name the packet gives it) and imports the pinned Tau Ceti declarations it reuses. The shared build has no object files for the Tau Ceti modules the file imports, so the file was not elaborated with its own import lines; the block, and the whole file, were elaborated at the pinned Mathlib with verbatim copies of the pinned Tau Ceti modules in place of those imports: no errors, and proof placeholders the only warnings. scripts/check_blueprint.py: 0 errors, 0 warnings. This review: (1) read all 88 L4 nodes against the authenticated NSW 2.3 (SHA-256 recorded; 5.1.9–5.1.10 and 5.3.19–5.3.20 with Exercises 1–3 re-read) and RJW, and found the mathematics right, including the corrected homology ranks (1,0,0)/(1,2,1) of (5.3.20); (2) added the 14 declarations and 8 missing test examples (12 records) to the suggested file, which elaborates at the pins with the admitted-proof placeholder as its only warning; (3) found three L2 nodes citing ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2/cartier-operators, a tier-5 roadmap, against WORKERS.md “Upstream tiers”, and planned the power-series Cartier operators here as L2/cartier-power-series (addedBy this job) with API, five tests and Lean signatures; the higher roadmap should import the power-series case from this node; (4) confirmed all 20 source findings at their locators (E13 printed field restated; it had described a text-extraction artefact); (5) confirmed all 537 baseline references by name and module in the pinned index and read the 12 entries new since round 1; (6) closed the two gaps that no longer hold (declaration/test correspondence; NSW authentication) and left the proof-input gaps 1–18 recorded; (7) checked that the reader describes all nodes and now the added one, and that L6 and the RT-AREA-iwasawa-2/4 contract are as the fix review verified. The 345 nodes of L0–L3 outside the edited ones were verified by the round-1 review and are unchanged; they were not re-read line by line here. Accepted as a complete pass under the node budget; every stage stays partial or not_read with its remaining list. Report: research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras~2.md.
